correctness.rationale: The Cartesian-product Laplacian spectral projectors yield the exact Moore-Penrose inverse H and H squared. Grounding one reference vertex and Schur-complementing two additional leaders yields an explicit 2-by-2 rational trace formula. Coordinate-equality partitions exhaust six triple orbits (three feasible at m=2). All five competitor-minus-matching rational functions have explicit positive denominators and numerators with positive coefficients after m=3+x,n=4+x+y; two-row competitors have two explicitly positive factored differences for n>=3. Exact rational optimum formulas and orbit counts were checked, with 37 independent direct grounded-Laplacian inverses. Finite checks supplement, but do not replace, the universal symbolic certificate; the theorem excludes square cases.

originality.rationale: A check against arbitrary-leader joint centrality, effective-resistance leader selection, published rook-graph algebra, related earlier two-leader and strongly regular three-leader results, and relevant indexed mathematical findings did not reveal an implication that classifies three leaders on strictly unequal complete-graph factors. The square strongly regular case is explicitly excluded because an earlier more general result covers it. The source identities and formulas for coherence are acknowledged, not claimed new; the sharp two-row versus at-least-three-row optimal-set classification and its exact values/counts are the distinct contribution. The conclusion is provisional relative to unindexed publications.

value.rationale: Exactly three noise-free sensor or actuator locations on the natural non-strongly-regular line graphs of K_{m,n} are classified globally for every pair of unequal factor sizes. The optimization exhibits a sharp finite feasibility transition at three rows: for two rows the optimal triple must share one row, whereas when at least three rows exist no two leaders share a row or column. The explicit rational optimal performance and exact numbers of solutions support placement design without combinatorial search. It is not a table recomputation or a single-size improvement; it is a complete infinite-family structural result and is distinct from previous square strongly regular coverage.
